identifier: L. B. Frechette, A. Baskaran, M. F. Hagan, "Active-noise-induced dynamic clustering of passive colloidal particles", Newton 1, 100167 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.newton.2025.100167. Values entered come from the Results text, the Fig. 1, 4, 8 and 9 captions, and Methods.
delivered_by: the person, as the publisher's PDF in ~/Downloads on the MacBook, named in task 039. Sixteen pages including references; the Supplemental Information (Figs. S1-S14, Notes S1-S2, videos) is online only and not in the file.
publication_status: PEER REVIEWED, CHECKED ON THE FILE. The PDF is the typeset version of record in Newton (Cell Press / Elsevier): received 20 February 2025, revised 3 May 2025, accepted 12 June 2025, published 14 July 2025, issue dated 8 September 2025.
grade_rule: E3, grade_tag peer_reviewed. Every result is a claim about the authors' MODEL: repulsive WCA particles, overdamped, advected by a Gaussian noise field correlated in space and time that stands in for an active fluid. The authors say themselves that the model is highly simplified and not expected to be quantitatively accurate, and the entries carry that.
license_note: Open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Identifier, stated conditions and numbers only; nothing of the text, figures or videos is reproduced.
method_as_stated: HOOMD-blue for the particle dynamics; the version is not stated. The active-noise generator is the authors' Python 3 code using CuPy on the GPU, joined to HOOMD-blue by a Python package of theirs; code at github.com/Layne28 (ActiveNoise, ActiveNoiseHoomd, active-assembly-hoomd, AnalysisTools) and a data and script archive on the Open Science Framework at https://osf.io/7ha8j/. MODEL: particles of diameter sigma interacting by a WCA potential of strength epsilon with cutoff 2^(1/6) sigma, overdamped, each displaced by minus the potential gradient plus the local noise-field value; no separate thermal noise term appears in the equation of motion. Reduced units: length sigma, energy epsilon, time t0 = gamma sigma^2/epsilon with gamma the friction coefficient. NOISE FIELD: Gaussian, zero mean, covariance va^2 exp(-|t-t'|/tau_a) exp(-|r-r'|/lambda_a) per Cartesian component; generated on a periodic grid by evolving each Fourier mode as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (Garcia-Ojalvo and Sancho), Euler-Maruyama in time, NumPy FFT, normalised so the variance is set by va alone; values between grid points by bilinear (2D) or trilinear (3D) interpolation; compressible by default, made incompressible by projecting out the longitudinal part with a discrete-grid correction. BOX 200 x 200 and noise-grid spacing 0.5 unless stated otherwise. SYSTEMS: 2D at packing fraction 0.1 (N = 5,016) and 0.4 (N = 20,372); 3D in a 64^3 box at 0.02 with a 128^3 grid (va = 1, lambda_a = 5, tau_a = 10). RUNS: random non-overlapping start, Euler-Maruyama time step 1e-4 for 250 time units, 50 independent runs per packing fraction and parameter set, configurations every time unit, error bars plus or minus two standard errors; clusters by a 1.2 distance cutoff. TRACER: time step 1e-2, mean squared displacement over 100 trajectories of 2,000 time units, fitted to the persistent-random-walk form. COST: one 2D trajectory of 2.5e6 steps with 20,372 particles and a 400 x 400 grid took about 1.5 hours on one AMD EPYC 7763 CPU and one NVIDIA A100 GPU (NERSC Perlmutter).
not_entered: Every value in the model's reduced units -- lambda_a, tau_a, va, time steps, run lengths, box size, the radius-of-gyration ratios (about 3.4 and 4.2 lambda_a for quenched noise at lambda_a = 20) -- because contracts/units.json registers no reduced length or time unit, and converting with a diameter the paper does not state is not permitted; they are in the note and above. The structure-factor peak scalings and the cluster-size distributions: figure-only (Figs. 6, 9, S8-S14). The experimental active-gel comparison (correlation length about 150 um and time about 1,100 s, used to map sigma = 15 um and t0 = 1,100 s): the velocity data are another group's, shown as an illustration of how the model's parameters would be read off an experiment, and are in the note rather than an entry.
note: Same group as Fang et al. 2020 (src_fang_2020_two_step_crystallization). The value for this repository is the recipe: correlated active noise as an external field added to overdamped dynamics in HOOMD-blue, with the generator published as code.
